decision: Use a dedicated read-only qrexec probe service that authenticates one bounded envelope and returns a deployment-bound Ed25519-attested response without opening MissionQueue, MissionStore, or DurableRequestJournal.
scope: Synthetic/defensive acceptance only. No real transactions, payment data, fraud workflows, or weakened controls.

correctness.reason: Proves qrexec framing/authentication/deployment identity independently from mission mutation semantics and makes zero-mutation auditable by construction.

robustnessSecurity.reason: The process has no MissionStore or request-journal dependency, rejects stale service/git/key identity, uses constant non-diagnostic stderr, and keeps HMAC plus Ed25519 verification fail-closed.

latencyResourceRegression.reason: One process, one request, one response, 16 KiB/32 KiB default bounds, no daemon/database/fsync/qrexec round trip beyond the probe itself, and no changes to MissionQueue/WorkerRuntime.

alternatives.name: Reuse mutable coordinator service with a no-op operation
alternatives.qa: Harder to prove zero mission-state interaction because service configuration and coordinator restore paths remain reachable.

alternatives.name: Dedicated read-only probe service
alternatives.qa: Clear fault isolation and zero MissionQueue dependencies by construction.

alternatives.name: Persistent qrexec probe daemon
alternatives.qa: Adds lifecycle/state/IPC surface with no value for the first acceptance gate.

qaAdded: valid authenticated probe returns request-bound Ed25519 attestation for exact service/git SHA/key ID
probe configuration does not require MissionStore or DurableRequestJournal paths
stale deployment identity fails closed before stdout
authentication failure and malformed framing fail closed
input limits fail closed and stderr does not reflect transport secret or request marker
knownLimit: Node-level tests cannot prove Qubes policy routing/denial itself. That remains a real-Qubes phase-1 acceptance item and must be demonstrated before any synthetic mission mutation across VMs.
failureLessons: A no-op added to a mutable coordinator service is weaker evidence than a service that cannot reach mission state at all.
Identity must bind service, exact Git SHA, and attestation key ID; transport authentication alone does not prove deployment freshness.
Policy denial is an external Qubes property and must not be falsely claimed from local process tests.
nextTask: Create the real-Qubes phase-1 invocation/policy evidence harness around the dedicated probe and require allow-only-intended-service plus deny-wrong-service evidence before synthetic claim/heartbeat/complete across VMs.
